input_description: AHF halo finder output with bundled MergerTree tool, ASCII format. 384^3 particle, 100 Mpc/h box dark-matter-only simulation. 129 snapshots, 5,766,243 halos, 151,996 trees.
issues_encountered: estimate_output.py's AHF snapshot-key regex grabbed the first digit run in the filename ('100' from '100Mpc_384_dmonly'), which is identical across all snapshot files, so max() ties and picked the alphabetically-first (near-empty, z=16.982) snapshot as 'latest', reporting n_trees_total=0

The registered driver's AHF_croco glob ('*.AHF_croco') matched 0 files because this dataset's MergerTree run used a different output prefix ('MTREE.code.<sim>.snap_NNN_croco', not '<sim>.AHF_croco'), silently producing 5,545,396 near-singleton trees with no real progenitor linkage instead of an error

No external snapshot scale-factor list existed for functional validation, and AHF_halos rows have no scale-factor/snap-index columns, so neither extract_snaplist.py mode (ascii column-scan or hdf5-output external-list) applied directly
resolutions: Manually confirmed the true latest snapshot (snap_128, 84,716 halos) via wc -l and reported the corrected trees estimate to the user at G1; the bug is in scripts/estimate_output.py (read-only during the session) and was not fixed in this session

Patched a copy of the driver in assets/drivers/ahf_mergetree_ascii.py, widening the glob to '*_croco' (matches the '_croco' suffix regardless of prefix). Confirmed via syntactic, functional, and semantic validation, then promoted to conversion-engine/drivers/ahf_mergetree_ascii.py in Stage 4
Built the snaplist directly from each .AHF_halos filename's embedded redshift (e.g. 'z0.000'), computing scale=1/(1+z) per snapshot and writing assets/<base>_snaplist.txt
